Bruyns Hill, Natal Midlands bioclimatic group 2; irrigated Hass on clonal Duke 7 rootstock, 7 x 7 m (200 trees/ha), planted 1982–1984. The paper reports Hass starting in its second season and Fuerte in its third. The two-to-three-year reference describes those trial cultivars, not every avocado or nursery starting age.

In this irrigated, intensively managed Natal Midlands trial, Hass reached about 20 t/ha at age 6 and orchards approached maximum sustainable average yield by age 8. This is a trial-specific bearing reference; there is no national plateau or automatically interpolated age-yield curve.

Same-trial arithmetic at the initial 200 trees/ha: 20,000 kg/ha / 200 = 100 kg/tree at age 6; sustainable average 22,500 kg/ha / 200 = 112.5 kg/tree. At age 3, 10,000 kg/ha / 200 = 50 kg/tree equivalent. These are average-equivalent reference values for the named Hass/Duke 7 orchard conditions, not measured individual-tree yields or default production for a different density, cultivar, climate or management. Intermediate ages are not inferred.

Hass on Duke 7, initially 200 trees/ha at Bruyns Hill (Natal Midlands bioclimatic group 2), with intensive irrigation and nutrition. Age 3: 10,000 kg/ha; age 6: 20,000 kg/ha; sustainable average about 22,500 kg/ha. Same-study density permits equivalents of 50 kg/tree at age 3 and 100 kg/tree at age 6; there is no reference for every intermediate age. These orchard benchmarks are conditional on good resources, comparable climate and timely orchard management, including Phytophthora control and thinning; do not auto-fill farm quantities.

Intermediate ages are not inferred.
